source_title: Beyond Delhi’s Diwali celebrations: 10 getaways for a royal stay, mountain air and quiet mornings - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Diwali in Delhi is a spectacular affair, with balconies glowing with fairy lights of every colour you can imagine, markets adorned with festive decorations, and how can we miss the never-ending sweet boxes? But the traffic, crowds on the streets and the unmissable pollution can make the festival feel like a lot. What if, this year, you swapped the familiar city celebrations for a little adventure? Whether you want a peaceful retreat, a family holiday or a road trip with friends, these ten getaways from Delhi offer a refreshing way to celebrate.1. Jaipur, Rajasthan â For a royal DiwaliApprox. 270â280 km from Delhi | 4â6 hours by roadIf you want to escape Delhi's pollution and winter around the time of Diwali but also want to remain at the centre of the festivities, Jaipur is the perfect getaway. Jaipur offers royal palaces and enormous forts, along with busy markets filled with handicrafts and Rajasthani sweets. Spend your days exploring the city's monuments, including Amer Fort, City Palace and Hawa Mahal. And, to get the festive feel, head to the markets for colourful textiles, blue pottery, jewellery and traditional sweets. The Rajasthani food will make your taste buds happy with a plate of pyaaz kachori followed by a glass of lassi. Moreover, the city's festive decorations can be spectacular.Best for: Families, culture lovers and festive shopping.2. Neemrana, Rajasthan â For a palace-style celebrationApprox. 120â130 km from Delhi | 2.5â3.5 hours by roadFor someone who wants to get away from the chaos that Indian roads experience during Diwali, a quiet hotel room can be comforting, making the most of the Diwali break. Neemrana Fort Palace offers just that, with its historic architecture and sweeping views of the Aravalli hills. The restored 15th-century fort makes a royal setting for a festive break, especially if you enjoy heritage stays.Check whether the property has special Diwali arrangements before booking; festive dinners and entertainment can vary.Best for: Couples, heritage enthusiasts and a luxurious short break.3. Rishikesh, Uttarakhand â For a quieter kind of celebrationApprox. 230â250 km from Delhi | 5â7 hours by roadThe holy city of Rishikesh is another option for a getaway during Diwali. The city offers a spiritual and adventurous experience. With the Ganga flowing in the background, one can have a peaceful time going on riverside walks, attending yoga sessions and visiting cafÃ©s. Attend the evening Ganga Aarti, explore the Beatles Ashram's graffiti-covered ruins or simply find a riverside spot to watch the gorgeous sunset over the hills.Adventure seekers can also look into rafting and other outdoor activities, depending on seasonal operations and local conditions.Best for: Nature lovers, wellness breaks and adventure enthusiasts.4. Agra, Uttar Pradesh â For history, romance and pethaApprox. 200â230 km from Delhi | 3â4 hours by roadAgra is an easy destination, with convenient travel from Delhi. The short trip is ideal for someone travelling with elderly parents or even fussy newborns. The city has great hotels and stays for a relaxing trip. The itinerary can include not just the Taj Mahal but also the historic city of Fatehpur Sikri and Agra's famous leather markets. If time permits, head to Mehtab Bagh for a different perspective of the Taj across the Yamuna. Do not miss the city's other main attraction: its food. From Mughlai specialities to the famous Agra petha, there is plenty to explore. A Diwali weekend here works particularly well for families and first-time visitors.Best for: Couples, families and history buffs.5. Lansdowne, Uttarakhand â For pine forests and peaceful morningsApprox. 250â280 km from Delhi | 5â7 hours by roadSome places are best explored with a checklist. Lansdowne is best explored without one. This quiet hill station, surrounded by pine and oak forests, is ideal for travellers who would rather wake up to birdsong than Diwali firecrackers.Take a gentle walk to Tip-in-Top for mountain views, visit St Mary's Church and spend some time around Bhulla Lake. The town's old-world cantonment atmosphere lends itself to a slow, restorative holiday.Best for: Couples, families and anyone seeking a break from city noise.6. Nainital, Uttarakhand â For a lakeside DiwaliApprox. 280â310 km from Delhi | 6â8 hours by roadThere is something wonderfully nostalgic about a hill-station holiday, and Nainital has all the ingredients: a beautiful lake, winding streets, mountain views and little shops selling things you never knew you needed. Start your morning with a boat ride on Naini Lake, visit Naina Devi Temple and take the cable car towards Snow View Point if the weather and operating conditions permit. When the evening chill sets in, wander along Mall Road, browse the local shops and find a cosy cafÃ© for a hot drink.Best for: Families, couples and classic mountain holidays.7. Bharatpur, Rajasthan â For a Diwali surrounded by birdsApprox. 180â200 km from Delhi | 3â4 hours by roadIf you would happily trade crowded markets for wetlands filled with birds, Bharatpur deserves a place on your list. Its biggest attraction is Keoladeo National Park, a celebrated wetland habitat that draws migratory birds during the cooler months.Rent a bicycle or explore with a local cycle-rickshaw guide, keeping an eye out for waterbirds, storks, kingfishers and other feathered visitors. October and November can be a rewarding time to explore. Bring binoculars to spot some of the spectacular birds.Best for: Birdwatchers, photographers, families and nature lovers.8. Mathura and Vrindavan, Uttar Pradesh â For a spiritually rich DiwaliApprox. 140â180 km from Delhi | 3â4 hours by roadInstead of a Diwali puja at home, this Diwali, take part in the festivities in the towns associated with Shri Krishna. Mathura and Vrindavan hold deep religious significance and offer a number of temple visits, along with Mathura's famous musical tradition.Visit Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura and Banke Bihari Mandir, ISKCON and Prem Mandir in Vrindavan. You can also explore the Yamuna ghats and local sweet shops, sampling peda and other traditional sweets.Best for: Families, spiritual travellers and those interested in Braj culture.9. Jim Corbett National Park, Uttarakhand â For a wild escapeApprox. 240â280 km from Delhi | 5â7 hours by roadTo spend the festival surrounded by natural beauty and wildlife, visit Jim Corbett National Park. Here, jeep safaris can offer the chance to spot a tiger, a deer or even a bear. You cannot enjoy Diwali firecrackers here, as the forest is a national park where activities are restricted to protect the natural environment.Best for: Wildlife enthusiasts, photographers and families with older children.10. Pushkar, Rajasthan â For desert colours and sunset walksApprox. 400â420 km from Delhi | 6â8 hours by roadPushkar is a little farther than the other destinations on this list, but the desert landscapes at the onset of winter make it worth the trip. The town offers a different side of Rajasthan, with the renowned Brahma Temple, Pushkar Lake and the unique handicrafts of the region. Pushkar is a lovely choice for travellers who want a festive escape that offers not just adventure but also a taste of folk culture.Best for: Couples, culture enthusiasts and slow travellers.You use AI every day.
